title: Unmasking the Fungal Menace: A Case Report of Chronic Granulomatous Invasive Fungal Sinusitis of Maxilla
content: Chronic granulomatous invasive fungal sinusitis (CGIFS) is an uncommon type of invasive sinusitis which is characteristically seen in immunocompetent individuals. Common clinical manifestations of this condition include proptosis, cheek swelling, and headache. The pathogenic organism is Aspergillus in majority of reported cases. Diagnosis is made by histopathological and microbiological examination of tissue specimens. Due to its expansible nature bone erosion is also associated with this condition. Treatment is surgical clearance/debulking followed by long term antifungal therapy. Here we report a case of 31 year old male presented with right side cheek swelling. Patient underwent medial maxillectomy and diagnosed as CGIFS. Patient was put on oral voriconazole for 3 months. To conclude CGIFS is rare variant of invasive fungal sinusitis which may mimic malignancy or granulomatous diseases such as tuberculosis, rhinoscleroma and rhinoscleroma. Accurate diagnosis is of utmost importance in providing management for CGIFS.
